sn11.20:0.3: The Worship of the Saṅgha (or Sakka’s Worship (3))
sn11.20:1.8: “Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, descending from the Vejayanta Palace, raised his joined hands in reverential salutation and worshipped the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
sn11.20:1.9: Then Matali the charioteer addressed Sakka, lord of the devas, in verse:
sn11.20:2.1: “‘It is these that should worship you—
sn11.20:2.2: The humans stuck in a putrid body,
sn11.20:3.1: Why then do you envy them,
sn11.20:3.3: Tell us about the seers’ conduct;
sn11.20:3.4: Let us hear what you have to say.’
sn11.20:4.1:
Sakka:
“‘This is why I envy them,
sn11.20:5.1: “‘They do not keep their goods in storage,
sn11.20:5.2: Neither in a pot nor in a box.
sn11.20:5.3: Seeking what has been prepared by others,
sn11.20:5.4: By this they live, firm in vows:
sn11.20:6.1: Those wise ones who give good counsel,
sn11.20:6.4: And people fight with one another,
sn11.20:7.1: Among those who fight, they do not fight;
sn11.20:7.2: Among the violent, they are quenched;
sn11.20:7.3: Among those who grasp, they do not grasp:
sn11.20:7.4: These are the ones whom I worship, Matali.’
sn11.20:8.1:
Matali:
“‘Those whom you worship, my lord Sakka,
sn11.20:8.2: Are indeed the best in the world.
sn11.20:9.1:
The Blessed One:
“Having given this explanation,
sn11.20:9.4: The chief, climbed into his chariot.”
